slides.title: ReactiveDynamics.jl Modeling Copilot
slides.subtitle: From a capacity-constrained business decision to a checked, reproducible model and a number you can defend, in a conversation, without anyone writing code.
slides.notes: Open with the value: a reusable capability, not a one-off model. The case at the end is a real blind-captured session.

slides.title: Capacity decisions need a model, and a model needs a modeler
slides.text:
- A launch reservation, a bid under a staffing ceiling, a portfolio competing for the same people: the answer depends on **who waits when the line is full**.
- A spreadsheet cannot represent a queue. Contention is an interaction between rows, and a spreadsheet's rows are independent by construction.
- So these questions go to a specialist, take weeks, and come back as a workbook the decision-maker has to take on faith.
- Most never get a model at all.
slides.notes: The bottleneck is not arithmetic, it is getting the question and the operation right.

slides.text: The interview runs in business language with the person who owns the decision. Every assumption lands in a brief they signed, including which inputs were their own estimates. The next question about the same operation starts from the same model.

slides.title: Four steps, and the third may stop the rest
slides.text:
| Step | You get | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| **Frame** | a signed brief | something must bind |
| **Author** | a checked model per option | validator silent |
| **Diagnose** | a health report | red check blocks |
| **Report** | estimate, mechanism, evidence | every number has a seed |

slides.title: The model is data, not code, so it can be checked before it runs
columns:
**Static checks.** A pure validator reads the model document and returns every problem with its exact path. A malformed model produces diagnostics, not a plausible wrong number. The language model proposes and a deterministic checker disposes, and the loop repeats until the checker is silent.

**Nothing generated is executed.** No `eval`, no generated scripts. Custom logic is one declared file.

**The IR.** The model is a closed, eval-free document: places that hold resources, transitions that hold them over time and sometimes fail, rates, costs, the arm deltas. It is diffable, serializable and replayable from `(model, seed)`.

**Checked again, for meaning.** Nine plausibility checks ask whether the scarce thing actually binds and whether the horizon cuts off the payoff.

**Guarded in CI.** The schema reference is generated from the engine, and a known-answer test re-derives a published result on every change.
slides.notes: Contrast with a code-writing assistant: code crashes or returns something, and something is the dangerous case.

slides.title: A thin layer over an engine that checks everything
slides.notes: Solid: shipped. Outlined: planned after endorsement (MCP W8, subagents W9, hook W10, plugin W12), adding reach, isolation and enforcement, not capability. No real MCP calls exist yet; these are drawn so the design is visible.

slides.title: Launch supply: do we pay for capacity before the readouts?
slides.subtitle: Blind-captured: two agents that cannot see each other's reasoning. The operator wrote its facts down before the first message. The company is invented, and the numbers are measurements.

slides.title: Two Phase-3 biologics, one fill-finish line, a CMO offer that expires 30 November

turns.text: Two Phase-3 biologics are coming. […] We have one sterile fill-finish line in-house, and most of it is already taken by our marketed products. It can probably carry one launch but not two. […] Our CFO says we shouldn't pay for capacity on an asset that has less than even odds.

**The CMO slot works for Tern's filing, but only just.** If you sign by 30 November, PPQ is done somewhere between late 2027 and early 2028. […] So the CMO can be Tern's filed site with no PAS, but only if the CMO runs on time and Tern doesn't read out early.
turns.call: python3 -c '<in-house headroom: 12.8 batches/mo minus marketed 9/mo growing 5%/yr>'

slides.notes: The operator's sheet flagged the validation rule as the thing people forget. The interview recovered it in turn 2.

slides.title: One model, an arm per option, calibrated to the operator's own figures
columns:
- `gen_models.py` writes one network; the arms differ only in parameters.
- `rdx validate`: 0 errors on every document.
- Calibration: Kestrel first-year revenue **$250.0M** against the operator's ~$250M, and **54** batches/yr at peak against 54.
- `rdx diagnose`: the own line binds (128 of 128 tenths used), and the design-dead branches are explained in `DOCTOR.md`.

- Options compared on **paired paths**: the same seed gives every option the same readout dates and lead times.
- Readout outcomes are forced per path and weighted by the stated odds (0.27 / 0.33 / 0.18 / 0.22).
- No option-level ensembles were run: a 96-seed ensemble took 53 minutes (W24). One wait ensemble served as a cross-check, and replays of three of its members matched exactly.

slides.title: Reserve now, review at Kestrel's readout, don't build
slides.notes: Build now is $73–105M worse even when both succeed. The Tern-only reservation, the operator's prior, leaves Kestrel short on every both-succeed path.
slides.text:
- **+$3.8M ± $1.1M** against waiting, odds-weighted; +$25M at peak-year batch value.
- **+$39M if both succeed** (27%): Tern short at launch on 26 of 37 paths under wait, 0 of 37 reserved.
- **A bounded $9–11M cost** in every other outcome.
- **Building is $73–105M worse** even when both succeed.
- The operator's prior, a Tern-only reservation, leaves Kestrel short on every both-succeed path.

slides.title: The model made the tail visible, and the owner supplied the option

turns.text: In the other outcomes the reservation costs money: Tern only, 0.18 chance, **−$18.6M to −$72.1M**. […] That is why the expected value nets to about zero.

Kestrel reads out in March 2027, nine months before Tern. […] I'd move Tern's PPQ in-house, file Tern on our own line, and give the CMO notice. That means eating the $5–10M. So the reservation isn't a fixed bet on Tern; it's something we decide to keep or drop at Kestrel's readout.
**Your guess holds: under the review rule, the Tern-only outcome costs $9.4M against waiting, and the $72M tail is gone.**
turns.call: python3 exit_review.py → weighted delta +3.81, se 1.10 (30 Tern-only paths)

slides.notes: From roughly break-even to +3.8 ± 1.1. The retraction was made out loud.

slides.title: What we are not claiming
slides.text:
- **The case is simulated.** Two role-playing agents; the operator was cooperative. It demonstrates the workflow, not anyone's supply plan.
- **Paired paths, not ensembles.** The run budget ruled ensembles out, and every figure says what it rests on.
- **The interview left soft inputs untested:** demand ±30%, marketed growth and readout correlation. The published facts audit leads with them.
- **The planned components are planned.** MCP, subagents, the hook and the plugin follow endorsement.
